text: @ada can you check the snapshot threshold?
why: A mention at the start of the text.
Handles are lowercased, deduplicated and sorted; the sentence's comma and full stop end the handle.
Dots inside a handle belong to it (the seed's generated handles have them); a trailing dot is punctuation.
Underscores and hyphens are handle characters, but trailing ones are dropped.
An @ after a letter is part of an email address, not a mention.
An @ after a letter or digit never starts a mention.
SQL's @@ operator: the first @ is not followed by a letter, the second follows an @.
A handle directly followed by another @ is an address.
An @ after / or = is inside a URL or an assignment.
Inline code spans are not scanned.
A span opened by two backticks closes only at the next run of exactly two, so the single backtick inside does not end it (CommonMark).
A backtick run with no matching closer is literal text, so the mention after it counts.
Brackets, quotes and emphasis markers may precede a mention.
A handle starts with an ASCII letter.
Handles are ASCII; a non-ASCII letter ends one. Real handles never contain one, so this only pins the grammar.
Any Unicode letter before the @ blocks the mention, not only ASCII ones.
A lone @ is not a mention.
